title: Making Sense of Ezekiel's Temple Vision
author: Steve Gregg
summary: Christian Research Journal column surveying literal-millennial, symbolic and other readings of Ezekiel 40–48, with attention to the problem of restored sacrifices.

title: Amillennial Interpretation of Ezekiel 40-48
author: Monergism.com (compiled article)
summary: Sets out the non-dispensational case that Ezekiel's temple vision is figurative and fulfilled in Christ and his people, pointing readers to Beale's temple theology.

title: The Temple and the Church's Mission: A Biblical Theology of the Dwelling Place of God
author: G. K. Beale
summary: Traces the temple theme from Eden to the new Jerusalem, reading Ezekiel 40–48 as fulfilled in Christ, the church and the new creation.

title: The Problem of Animal Sacrifices in Ezekiel 40–48 (Bibliotheca Sacra 152)
author: Jerry M. Hullinger
summary: Dispensational proposal that millennial sacrifices effect ceremonial (not soteriological) cleansing so that God's presence can dwell among mortals.
note: Bibliographic details from memory; not confirmed online in this session.

title: The Prophecy of Ezekiel: The Glory of the Lord
author: Charles L. Feinberg
summary: Dispensational commentary defending a literal future regathering of Israel and a millennial temple.

title: The Book of Ezekiel, Chapters 25–48 (NICOT)
author: Daniel I. Block
summary: Major evangelical commentary; reads chs. 40–48 as an ideological-theological vision of restored divine presence rather than a building blueprint.

title: Preterism and Zechariah 12–14
author: Thomas D. Ice
summary: Pre-Trib Research Center article arguing that Zechariah 12–14 cannot be fulfilled in AD 70, since there God rescues Jerusalem rather than judging it.

title: The Footsteps of the Messiah: A Study of the Sequence of Prophetic Events (rev. ed.)
author: Arnold G. Fruchtenbaum
summary: Messianic-Jewish dispensational synthesis that makes Israel's national confession (Zechariah 12:10; Hosea 5:15) the trigger of the Second Coming.

title: Paradise Restored: A Biblical Theology of Dominion
author: David Chilton
summary: Popular Reconstructionist postmillennial biblical theology reading Eden, Ezekiel 47 and the prophets as promises of the gospel's growing global triumph.

title: The Days of Vengeance: An Exposition of the Book of Revelation
author: David Chilton
summary: Early-date, covenantal-preterist commentary reading Revelation as God's covenant lawsuit against apostate Jerusalem.

title: The Greatness of the Great Commission: The Christian Enterprise in a Fallen World
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Argues that Matthew 28:18–20 commissions the discipling of nations as nations and implies the commission's historical success.

title: The Gospel of the Kingdom: Scriptural Studies in the Kingdom of God
author: George Eldon Ladd
summary: Lectures presenting the kingdom as God's reign present in mystery now and coming in power at the Second Advent; includes the parables of Matthew 13.

title: The Presence of the Future: The Eschatology of Biblical Realism
author: George Eldon Ladd
summary: Ladd's scholarly case for inaugurated eschatology (already/not yet) in Jesus's teaching.

title: The Coming of the Kingdom
author: Herman Ridderbos
summary: Reformed biblical-theological study of the kingdom in the Synoptics, stressing fulfilment-in-stages between Jesus's resurrection and the Parousia.

title: Matthew (Expositor's Bible Commentary, vol. 8)
author: D. A. Carson
summary: Evangelical commentary with extended discussion of Matthew 10:23, 16:28 and chapter 24.

title: The Interpretation of Matthew 10:23b (Detroit Baptist Seminary Journal 24)
author: Ryan E. Meyer
summary: Surveys readings of Matthew 10:23b from Schweitzer onward, including AD 70, resurrection and Second Coming interpretations.

title: Some Standing Here Will Not Taste Death
author: Keith A. Mathison
summary: Part of Ligonier's 'Unfolding of Biblical Eschatology' series; lists transfiguration, resurrection-Pentecost, AD 70 and Second Coming readings of Matthew 16:28 and leans to the transfiguration.

title: The Elements Shall Melt with Fervent Heat (formerly 2 Peter 3: The Late Great Kingdom)
author: Don K. Preston
summary: Covenant-eschatology exposition reading 2 Peter 3 as the passing of the old covenant world in AD 70.
note: Title confirmed via search snippets; publication year not confirmed.

title: Acts (Baker Exegetical Commentary on the New Testament)
author: Darrell L. Bock
summary: Progressive-dispensational commentary that reads Acts 1:6–7 and 3:19–21 as keeping a future restoration for Israel in view.

title: The Case for Progressive Dispensationalism
author: Robert L. Saucy
summary: Argues for one unfolding kingdom program with a future national role for Israel, inaugurated now and completed at Christ's return.

title: 2 Peter 3 and the Consummation (1)
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Gentry, a partial preterist, argues against AD 70 readings that 2 Peter 3 describes the final conflagration and consummate new creation at the Second Advent.

title: The Promise of His Appearing: An Exposition of Second Peter
author: Peter J. Leithart
summary: Reads the 'heavens and earth' that pass away in 2 Peter 3 as the old covenant order ended in AD 70.

title: Providential Changes, an Argument for Universal Holiness (sermon on 2 Peter 3:11)
author: John Owen
summary: Puritan sermon applying the dissolving 'heavens and earth' of 2 Peter 3 to the Jewish church-state; often cited by preterists.
note: Title and date from memory (Owen's Works, vol. 9); not confirmed online in this session.

title: Jude, 2 Peter (Word Biblical Commentary 50)
author: Richard J. Bauckham
summary: Standard critical-evangelical commentary on 2 Peter 3, including the text-critical problem at 3:10.

title: Hebrews 1–8 and Hebrews 9–13 (Word Biblical Commentary 47A–B)
author: William L. Lane
summary: Major commentary dating Hebrews in the 60s and reading 8:13 and 12:26–28 in light of the passing old order.

title: The Resurrection of the Son of God
author: N. T. Wright
summary: Historical study arguing that resurrection in Second Temple Judaism and the NT meant bodily life after death, including Daniel 12:2 and John 5:28–29.

title: A Critique of the Preterist View of Revelation 17:9–11 and Nero (Bibliotheca Sacra 164)
author: Mark L. Hitchcock
summary: Futurist rebuttal of the early-date argument from the seven kings of Revelation 17.

title: Revelation in Nero's Time
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Presents the seven-kings count (Julius to Nero as sixth, Galba seventh) as the leading internal evidence for a pre-70 date.

title: The Climax of Prophecy: Studies on the Book of Revelation
author: Richard Bauckham
summary: Includes a long study of Nero, the Nero redivivus legend and the gematria of 666 (Nero Caesar and 'beast' both 666 in Hebrew letters).

title: P115 and the Number of the Beast (Tyndale Bulletin 58.1)
author: P. J. Williams
summary: Notes the 616 reading in P115, the oldest papyrus of Revelation 13, and suggests a scribal visual echo alongside the Nero explanation.

title: Beastly Number
author: Peter J. Leithart
summary: Essay discussing Bauckham's Nero gematria and James Jordan's alternative linking 666 to Solomon's gold (1 Kings 10:14).

title: Revelation 13:18 and a Scroll from Murabba'at (BASOR 170)
author: Delbert R. Hillers
summary: Publishes the Aramaic spelling nrwn qsr from a Murabba'at document, supporting the Hebrew-letter Nero gematria.
note: Bibliographic details from memory; not confirmed online in this session.

title: Revelation (Word Biblical Commentary 52A–C)
author: David E. Aune
summary: Massive critical commentary; treats the Nero legend, 666/616 and the seven kings in detail.

title: Revelation 8–22: An Exegetical Commentary
author: Robert L. Thomas
summary: Detailed dispensational futurist commentary reading the beast as a future individual ruler.

title: The Returning King: A Guide to the Book of Revelation
author: Vern S. Poythress
summary: Reformed amillennial guide reading Revelation's visions as symbolic depictions of the conflict between Christ and evil throughout the church age.

title: A New Heaven and a New Earth: Reclaiming Biblical Eschatology
author: J. Richard Middleton
summary: Argues for a holistic eschatology of cosmic renewal rather than annihilation, including Revelation 21–22 and 2 Peter 3:10.

title: The Letters to Timothy and Titus (NICNT)
author: Philip H. Towner
summary: Commentary reading the 'last days' of 2 Timothy 3:1 as the present era already under way in Ephesus.
